intro: 3.13 added two small but useful standard-library features: copy.replace() unifies "copy with some fields changed", and warnings.deprecated (PEP 702) makes a retired API warn at run time and get flagged by type checkers.
example_desc: PointConfig is a frozen dataclass; copy.replace() returns a new object with a different scale and leaves the original untouched. With @deprecated, every call to read_point() emits a DeprecationWarning and type checkers flag the call site.

case.title: Changing one point's scale changed every point sharing its config
paragraphs: A program kept point settings in mutable objects. To try a new scale someone set cfg.scale directly, and every point referencing the same object changed with it; the reports were wrong for a whole day. With frozen dataclasses and copy.replace(), a change can only create a new object.

Another common problem is old APIs that can never be removed because nobody knows who still calls them. @deprecated makes callers see the warning immediately in tests (run with -W error::DeprecationWarning) and in the editor.
steps: Use frozen=True dataclasses for configuration objects.
Create variants with copy.replace() instead of mutating the original.
Mark functions being retired with @deprecated, naming the replacement and the removal version.
Run CI tests with -W error::DeprecationWarning to find remaining callers.

updates.text: Python 3.13 moved to security-only fixes in October 2026 and is expected to reach end of life in October 2029. On 3.12 and earlier, typing_extensions.deprecated provides the same decorator.

sources.title: Python Developer's Guide: Status of Python versions

exercises.a: Any object implementing __replace__. In the standard library that includes dataclasses, namedtuples, datetime, date, time, SimpleNamespace and code objects. Custom classes gain support by defining __replace__.
It raises TypeError: a dataclass's __replace__ calls the constructor with the new arguments, and PointConfig has no unit field.

exercises.q: Why does the example use catch_warnings(record=True) with simplefilter("always")?
exercises.a: By default a DeprecationWarning is shown only when triggered from __main__, and only once per location. Recording with "always" makes the example capture and print the warning reliably.

exercises.q: Why is the result of read_points {'SAT': 2.25}, with only one entry?
exercises.a: Both configs are named SAT, so the second value (225 × 0.01 = 2.25) overwrites the first (22.5) under the same key. In practice point names must be unique; check this when loading configuration.
